**Artificial intelligence** (**AI**) is the capability of [computational systems](#Privacy_and_copyright "Contents") to perform tasks typically associated with [human intelligence](#Dominance_by_tech_giants "Contents"), such as [learning](#Dominance_by_tech_giants "Contents"), [reasoning](#Dominance_by_tech_giants "Contents"), [problem-solving](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents"), [perception](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents"), and [decision-making](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents"). It is a field of research in [engineering](#Misinformation "Contents"), [mathematics](#Misinformation "Contents"), and [computer science](#Misinformation "Contents") that develops and studies methods and [software](#Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness "Contents") that enable machines to perceive their environment and use [learning](#Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness "Contents") and [intelligence](#Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness "Contents") to take actions that maximise their chances of achieving defined
goals.[[1]](#Technological_unemployment "Contents")

High-profile [applications of AI](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents") include advanced [web search engines](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents"), [chatbots](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents"), [virtual assistants](#Existential_risk "Contents"), [autonomous vehicles](#Existential_risk "Contents"), play and analysis in [strategy games](#Existential_risk "Contents") (e.g., [chess](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents") and [Go](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents")), and [content generation](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents") (e.g. images, audio, and videos).

The traditional goals of AI research include learning, [reasoning](#Open_source "Contents"), [knowledge representation](#Open_source "Contents"), [planning](#Frameworks "Contents"), [natural language processing](#Frameworks "Contents"), and [perception](#Regulation "Contents"), as well as support for [robotics](#Regulation
"Contents").[[a]](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents") To reach these goals,
AI researchers use techniques including [state space search](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents") and [mathematical optimisation](#Legal_definitions "Contents"), [formal logic](#Legal_definitions "Contents"), [artificial neural networks](#Evaluating_approaches_to_AI "Contents"), and methods based on [statistics](#Evaluating_approaches_to_AI "Contents"), [operations research](#Evaluating_approaches_to_AI "Contents"), and [economics](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits
"Contents").[[b]](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents") AI also draws upon [psychology](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents"), [linguistics](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents"), [philosophy](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents"), [neuroscience](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents"), and other
fields.[[2]](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents") Some companies,
such as [OpenAI](#Consciousness "Contents"), [Google DeepMind](#Consciousness "Contents"), and [Meta](#Consciousness "Contents"), aim to create [artificial general intelligence](#Computationalism_and_functionalism "Contents") (AGI)—AI that can complete nearly any [cognitive](#Computationalism_and_functionalism "Contents") task at least as well as a
human.[[3]](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents")

Artificial intelligence was founded as an [academic discipline](#Future "Contents") in 1956.[[4]](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents")
The field went through multiple cycles of optimism throughout [its history](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity
"Contents"),[[5]](#Transhumanism "Contents")[[6]](#In_fiction "Contents") followed
by periods of disappointment and loss of funding, known as [AI winters](#See_also "Contents").[[7]](#Explanatory_notes
"Contents")[[8]](#References "Contents") Funding and interest increased substantially
after 2012, when [graphics processing units](#Further_reading "Contents") (GPUs) started being used to accelerate neural networks, and [deep learning](#Textbooks "Contents") outperformed previous AI
techniques.[[9]](#Textbooks "Contents") This growth accelerated further after 2017
with the [transformer architecture](#History_of_AI "Contents").[[10]](#External_links "Contents")
In the 2020s, an [AI boom](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents") coincided with advances in [generative AI](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents"), which became widespread and allowed for the creation and modification of media. In addition to [AI safety](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown vector-page-titlebar-toc vector-button-flush-left") and [unintended consequences and harms](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Table of Contents") from the use of AI, [ethical concerns](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown-checkbox "), [AI's long-term effects](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown-label cdx-button cdx-button--fake-button cdx-button--fake-button--enabled cdx-button--weight-quiet cdx-button--icon-only "), [environmental effects](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie
"vector-unpinned-container"),[[11]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "p-lang-btn")
and [potential existential risks](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans") have prompted discussions of [AI regulation](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans").


## Goals

The general problem of simulating (or creating) intelligence has been broken down
into subproblems. These consist of specific traits or capabilities that researchers
expect an intelligent system to display. The traits described below have received
the most attention and cover the scope of AI research.[[a]](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%88%B0%E1%8B%8D_%E1%88%A0%E1%88%AB%E1%88%BD_%E1%8B%A8%E1%88%9B%E1%88%B0%E1%89%A5_%E1%89%BD%E1%88%8E%E1%89%B3 "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic")


### Reasoning and problem-solving

Early researchers developed algorithms that imitated step-by-step reasoning that
humans use when solving puzzles or making logical [deductions](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelichencia_artificial "Intelichencia artificial –
Aragonese").[[12]](https://anp.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AE_%E0%A4%AC%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%BF "कृत्रिम बुद्धि – Angika")
By the late 1980s and 1990s, methods were developed for dealing with [uncertain](anp "कृत्रिम बुद्धि") or incomplete information, employing concepts from [probability](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic") and [economics](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "ذكاء اصطناعي –
Arabic").[[13]](https://ary.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%AF%D9%83%D8%A7_%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan Arabic")

Many of these [algorithms](ary "دكا صطيناعي") were insufficient for solving large reasoning problems because they experienced a "combinatorial explosion", meaning they become exponentially slower as the problems
grow.[[14]](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese")
Even humans rarely use the step-by-step deduction that early AI research could model.
Humans solve most of their problems using fast, intuitive judgments.[[15]](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%BCni_intellekt "Süni intellekt – Azerbaijani")

[Reasoning models](https://azb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D9%85%D8%B5%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B9%DB%8C_%D8%B0%DA%A9%D8%A7 "مصنوعی ذکا – South Azerbaijani"), a type of [large language model](https://azb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D9%85%D8%B5%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B9%DB%8C_%D8%B0%DA%A9%D8%A7 "مصنوعی ذکا – South Azerbaijani") (LLM) trained to generate intermediate chains-of-thought, emerged in 2024 and allowed improved performance on complex problems in mathematics and
coding.[[16]](ba "Яһалма интеллект – Bashkir") These models can
produce incorrect outputs or "[hallucinations](https://bar.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinschtlicha_Intelligenz "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz – Bavarian")," unlike symbolic [reasoning systems](bar "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz –
Bavarian").[[17]](sgs "Dėrbtėns intelekts")


### Knowledge representation
[![Tuigse inntealta – Scottish Gaelic](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)")](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B_%D1%96%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%8D%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)")
An ontology represents knowledge as a set of concepts within a domain and the relationships
between those concepts.
AI programs use knowledge to answer questions intelligently and make deductions about
real-world facts.

Formal [knowledge representation](https://bew.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calakan_bikinan "Calakan bikinan – Betawi") and [knowledge engineering](bew "Calakan bikinan – Betawi") use [symbols](https://bg.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B7%D0%BA%D1%83%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%B5%D0%BD_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Изкуствен интелект – Bulgarian") to represent words, concepts and things in the
world.[[18]](https://bh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9F%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AB%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B2_%E0%A4%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%B8 "आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस –
Bhojpuri")[[c]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
A [knowledge base](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") is a body of knowledge represented in a form that can be used by a program. An [ontology](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") is the set of objects, relations, concepts, and properties used by a particular domain of
knowledge.[[24]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
Formal knowledge has been studied extensively since the 1970s and researchers have
developed formalisms for a wide variety of difficult domains.[[d]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

The symbolic approach has difficulty with several problems: the breadth of [commonsense knowledge](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (the set of atomic facts the average person knows is
enormous),[[30]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
the sub-symbolic form of most commonsense knowledge (much of what people know is
not represented as "facts" or "statements" they can express verbally),[[15]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
and [knowledge acquisition](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (the problem of obtaining knowledge for AI
applications).[[e]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

[Large language models](//upload.wikimedia.org "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (and some other AI programs developed since 2012) do not require explicit, symbolic knowledge. They acquire knowledge by being trained on the combined text of millions of books and billions of websites. Modern AI can also learn about a domain by running experiments (as when [AlphaZero](//upload.wikimedia.org "Wikipedia (en)") learns game strategy by playing against itself). [Machine learning](/w/rest.php/v1/search "Wikipedia (en)") solves the problems of general knowledge, commonsense knowledge and knowledge acquisition, however this approach has struggled with accurate recall and valid
reasoning.[*[citation needed](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=")*]


### Planning and decision-making

An "agent" is any entity (artificial or not) that perceives and takes actions in
the world. A [rational agent](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") has goals or preferences and takes actions to make them happen.[[f]](#bodyContent "Main
menu")[[33]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") In [automated planning](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), the agent has a specific
goal.[[34]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") In [automated decision-making](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), the agent has preferences—there are some situations it would prefer to be in, and some situations it is trying to avoid. The decision-making agent assigns a number to each situation (called its "[utility](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")") that measures how much the agent prefers it. For each possible action, it can calculate the "[expected utility](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")": the utility of all possible outcomes of the action, weighted by the probability that the outcome will occur. It can then choose the action with the maximum expected
utility.[[35]](/wiki/Wikipedia:About "Learn about Wikipedia and how it works")

In [classical planning](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us "How to contact Wikipedia"), the agent knows exactly what the effect of any action will
be.[[36]](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia") In
most real-world problems, however, the agent may not be certain about the situation
it is in (it is "unknown" or "unobservable") and it may not know for certain what
will happen after each possible action (it is not "deterministic"). It must choose
an action by making a probabilistic guess and then reassess the situation to see
if the action worked.[[37]](/wiki/Special:SpecialPages "A list of all special pages [q]")

Alongside thorough testing and improvement based on previous decisions, having an
explanation for why the agent took certain decisions is a way to build trust, especially
when the decisions have to be relied upon.[[38]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")

In some problems, the agent's preferences may be uncertain, especially if there are
other agents or humans involved. These preferences may be learned (e.g., with [inverse reinforcement learning](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")), or the agent can seek information to improve
them.[[39]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
[Information value theory](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]") can be used to weigh the value of exploratory or experimental
actions.[[40]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
The space of possible future actions and situations is typically [intractably](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color") large, so the agents must take actions and evaluate situations while being uncertain of the outcome.

A [Markov decision process](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color") has a [transition model](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color") that describes the probability that a particular action will change the state in a particular way and a reward function that supplies the utility of each state and the cost of each action. A [policy](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") associates a decision with each possible state. The policy could be calculated (e.g., by [policy iteration](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")), determined by a [heuristic](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title="), or
learned.[[41]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")

[Game theory](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") describes the rational behaviour of multiple interacting agents and is used in AI programs that make decisions involving other
agents.[[42]](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")


### Learning

[Machine learning](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options") is the study of programs that can improve their performance on a given task
automatically.[[43]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")
It has been a part of AI from the beginning.[[g]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
[![vector-toc-list-item vector-toc-level-2](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail " title=")](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
In [supervised learning](# "Contents"), the training data is labelled with the expected answers, while in [unsupervised learning](# "Contents"), the model identifies patterns or structures in unlabelled data.
There are several kinds of machine learning:

- [Unsupervised learning](# "Contents") analyses a stream of data, finds patterns, and makes predictions without any other guidance.[[46]](# "Contents")
- [Supervised learning](# "Contents") requires labelling the training data with the expected answers, and comes in two main varieties: [classification](#Goals "Contents") (where the program must learn to predict what category the input belongs in) and [regression](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents") (where the program must deduce a numeric function based on numeric input).[[47]](#Knowledge_representation "Contents")
- [Reinforcement learning](#Knowledge_representation "Contents") is when the agent is rewarded for good responses and punished for bad ones. The agent learns to choose responses that are classified as "good".[[48]](#Learning "Contents")
- [Transfer learning](#Learning "Contents") is when the knowledge gained from one problem is applied to a new problem.[[49]](#Perception "Contents")
- [Deep learning](#Perception "Contents") is a type of machine learning that runs inputs through biologically inspired [artificial neural networks](#Social_intelligence "Contents") for all of these types of learning.[[50]](#General_intelligence "Contents")

[Computational learning theory](#General_intelligence "Contents") can assess learners by [computational complexity](#Techniques "Contents"), [sample complexity](#Techniques "Contents") (how much data is required), or other notions of [optimisation](#Search_and_optimisation
"Contents").[[51]](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents")


### Natural language processing

[Natural language processing](#Local_search "Contents") (NLP) allows programs to read, write, and communicate in human
languages.[[52]](#Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning "Contents") Specific
problems include [speech recognition](#Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning "Contents"), [speech synthesis](#Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods "Contents"), [machine translation](#Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods "Contents"), [information extraction](#Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods "Contents"), [information retrieval](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents"), and [question answering](#Artificial_neural_networks
"Contents").[[53]](#Deep_learning "Contents")

Early work, based on [Noam Chomsky](#Deep_learning "Contents")'s [generative grammar](#GPT "Contents") and [semantic networks](#GPT "Contents"), had difficulty with [word-sense disambiguation](#Hardware_and_software
"Contents")[[h]](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") unless restricted
to small domains called "[micro-worlds](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents")" (due to the [common sense knowledge problem](#AI-assisted_software_development
"Contents")[[30]](#Chatbots "Contents")). British [linguist](#Physical_AI "Contents") and philosopher [Margaret Masterman](#Health_and_medicine "Contents") believed it was meaning and not grammar that was the key to understanding
languages,[[54]](#Gaming "Contents") and that dictionaries and especially [thesauri](#Mathematics "Contents") should be the basis of computational language
structure.[[55]](#Finance "Contents")

Modern deep learning techniques for NLP include [word embedding](#Military "Contents") (representing words, typically as [vectors](#Military "Contents") encoding their
meaning),[[56]](#Web_search "Contents") [transformers](#Sexuality "Contents") (a deep learning architecture using an [attention](#Sexuality "Contents")
mechanism),[[57]](#Risks_and_harm "Contents") and others.[[58]](#Risks_and_harm "Contents")
In 2019, [generative pre-trained transformer](#Privacy_and_copyright "Contents") (or "GPT") language models began to generate coherent
text.[[59]](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents")[[60]](#Lack_of_transparency "Contents")
By 2023, these models were able to get human-level scores on the [bar exam](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents"), [SAT](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents") (Scholastic Assessment Test), [GRE](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents") (Graduate Record Examination), and many other real-world
applications.[[61]](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents")


### Perception

[Machine perception](#Existential_risk "Contents") is the ability to use input from sensors (such as cameras, microphones, wireless signals, active [lidar](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents"), [sonar](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents"), [radar](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents"), and [tactile sensors](#Open_source "Contents")) to deduce aspects of the world. [Computer vision](#Open_source "Contents") is the ability to analyse visual
input.[[62]](#Frameworks "Contents")

The field includes [speech recognition](#Regulation "Contents"),[[63]](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents")
[image classification](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents"),[[64]](#Evaluating_approaches_to_AI "Contents")
[facial recognition](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits "Contents"), [object recognition](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits
"Contents"),[[65]](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents") [object tracking](#Narrow_vs._general_AI
"Contents"),[[66]](#Computationalism_and_functionalism "Contents") and [robotic perception](#AI_welfare_and_rights
"Contents").[[67]](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents")


### Social intelligence
[![Tuigse inntealta – Scottish Gaelic](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Transhumanism "Contents")
[Kismet](#See_also "Contents"), a robot head made in the 1990s, is a machine that can recognise and simulate
emotions.[[68]](#References "Contents")
[Affective computing](#Further_reading "Contents") is a field that comprises systems that recognise, interpret, process, or simulate human [affect](#Textbooks "Contents") (feeling, emotion, and
mood).[[69]](#Textbooks "Contents") For example, some [virtual assistants](#History_of_AI "Contents") are programmed to speak conversationally or even banter humorously; it makes them appear more sensitive to the emotional dynamics of human interaction, or to otherwise facilitate [human–computer interaction](#Other_sources "Contents").

However, this tends to give naïve users an unrealistic conception of the intelligence
of existing computer agents.[[70]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents")
Moderate successes related to affective computing include textual [sentiment analysis](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "button") and, more recently, [multimodal sentiment analysis](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-page-titlebar-toc-checkbox"), wherein AI classifies the effects displayed by a videotaped
subject.[[71]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans")


### General intelligence

A machine with [artificial general intelligence](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans") (AGI) would be able to solve a wide variety of problems with breadth and versatility similar to [human intelligence](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie –
Afrikaans").[[72]](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%88%B0%E1%8B%8D_%E1%88%A0%E1%88%AB%E1%88%BD_%E1%8B%A8%E1%88%9B%E1%88%B0%E1%89%A5_%E1%89%BD%E1%88%8E%E1%89%B3 "Künstliche Intelligenz")


## Techniques

AI research uses a wide variety of techniques to accomplish the goals above.[[b]](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic")


### Search and optimisation

There are two different kinds of search used in AI: [state space search](https://ary.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%AF%D9%83%D8%A7_%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan Arabic") and [local search](ary "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan Arabic"):


#### State space search

[State space search](https://arz.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%89 "ذكاء صناعى – Egyptian Arabic") searches through a tree of possible states to try to find a goal
state.[[73]](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese")
For example, [planning](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা") algorithms search through trees of goals and subgoals, attempting to find a path to a target goal, a process called [means-ends analysis](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelixencia_artificial "Intelixencia artificial –
Asturian").[[74]](https://ba.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%AF%D2%BB%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BC%D0%B0_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "مصنوعی ذکا")

[Simple exhaustive searches](https://ba.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%AF%D2%BB%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BC%D0%B0_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Яһалма интеллект –
Bashkir")[[75]](https://bar.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinschtlicha_Intelligenz "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz – Bavarian")
are rarely sufficient for most real-world problems: the [search space](https://bat-smg.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%97rbt%C4%97ns_intelekts "Dėrbtėns intelekts – Samogitian") (the number of places to search) quickly grows to [astronomical numbers](https://bat-smg.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%97rbt%C4%97ns_intelekts "Dėrbtėns intelekts – Samogitian"). The result is a search that is [too slow](https://bcl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artipisyal_na_intelihensya "Artipisyal na intelihensya – Central Bikol") or never
completes.[[14]](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B_%D1%96%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%8D%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)")
"[Heuristics](be-tarask "Штучны інтэлект")" or "rules of thumb" can help prioritise choices that are more likely to reach a
goal.[[76]](be "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian")

[Adversarial search](https://bew.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calakan_bikinan "Calakan bikinan – Betawi") is used for [game-playing](https://bew.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calakan_bikinan "Calakan bikinan – Betawi") programs, such as chess or Go. It searches through a [tree](https://bg.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%98%D0%B7%D0%BA%D1%83%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%B5%D0%BD_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Изкуствен интелект – Bulgarian") of possible moves and countermoves, looking for a winning
position.[[77]](https://bh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9F%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AB%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B2_%E0%A4%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%B8 "आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस – Bhojpuri")


#### Local search
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")
Illustration of [gradient descent](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") for three different starting points; two parameters (represented by the plan coordinates) are adjusted in order to minimise the [loss function](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") (the height).
[Local search](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") uses [mathematical optimisation](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") to find a solution to a problem. It begins with some form of guess and refines it
incrementally.[[78]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

[Gradient descent](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") is a type of local search that optimises a set of numerical parameters by incrementally adjusting them to minimise a [loss function](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"). Variants of gradient descent are commonly used to train [neural networks](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia"),[[79]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
through the [backpropagation](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") algorithm.

Another type of local search is [evolutionary computation](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), which aims to iteratively improve a set of candidate solutions by "mutating" and "recombining" them, [selecting](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") only the fittest to survive each
generation.[[80]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

Distributed search processes can coordinate via [swarm intelligence](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") algorithms. Two popular swarm algorithms used in search are [particle swarm optimisation](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (inspired by bird [flocking](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")) and [art colony optimisation](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (inspired by [ant trails](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia")).[[81]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")


### Logic

Formal [logic](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") is used for [reasoning](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") and [knowledge representation](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia").[[82]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia")Formal logic comes in two main forms: [propositional logic](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (which operates on statements that are true or false and uses [logical connectives](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") such as "and", "or", "not" and
"implies")[[83]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
and [predicate logic](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (which also operates on objects, predicates and relations and uses [quantifiers](//upload.wikimedia.org "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") such as
"*Every* *X* is a *Y*" and "There are *some* *X*s that are *Y*s").[[84]](/w/rest.php/v1/search "Wikipedia (en)")

[Deductive reasoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Wikipedia Atom feed") in logic is the process of [proving](/w/index.php?title=Special:RecentChanges&feed=atom "Wikipedia Atom feed") a new statement ([conclusion](//meta.wikimedia.org "></script></head>
<body class=")) from other statements that are given and assumed to be true (the [premises](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=")).[[85]](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") Proofs can be structured as proof [trees](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="), in which nodes are labelled by sentences, and children nodes are connected to parent nodes by [inference rules](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=").

Given a problem and a set of premises, problem-solving reduces to searching for a
proof tree whose root node is labelled by a solution of the problem and whose [leaf nodes](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") are labelled by premises or [axioms](#bodyContent "Main menu"). In the case of [Horn clauses](#bodyContent "Main menu"), problem-solving search can be performed by reasoning [forwards](#bodyContent "Main menu") from the premises or [backwards](#bodyContent "Main menu") from the
problem.[[86]](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu") In the more general case of the clausal
form of [first-order logic](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu"), [resolution](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") is a single, axiom-free rule of inference, in which a problem is solved by proving a contradiction from premises that include the negation of the problem to be
solved.[[87]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")

Inference in both Horn clause logic and first-order logic is [undecidable](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), and therefore [intractable](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"). However, backward reasoning with Horn clauses, which underpins computation in the [logic programming](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") language [Prolog](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), is [Turing complete](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"). Moreover, its efficiency is competitive with computation in other [symbolic programming](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
languages.[[88]](/wiki/Portal:Current_events "Articles related to current events")

[Fuzzy logic](/wiki/Special:Random "Visit a randomly selected article [x]") assigns a "degree of truth" between 0 and 1. It can therefore handle propositions that are vague and partially
true.[[89]](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia")

[Non-monotonic logics](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia"), including logic programming with [negation as failure](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Learn how to edit Wikipedia"), are designed to handle [default reasoning](/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "The hub for
editors").[[29]](/wiki/Special:SpecialPages "Add images or other media for use on Wikipedia")
Other specialised versions of logic have been developed to describe many complex
domains.


### Probabilistic methods for uncertain reasoning
[![vector-toc-list-item vector-toc-level-2](/static/images/mobile/copyright/wikipedia-tagline-en-25.svg "Search Wikipedia [f]")](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")
A simple [Bayesian network](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]"), with the associated [conditional probability tables](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
Many problems in AI (including reasoning, planning, learning, perception, and robotics)
require the agent to operate with incomplete or uncertain information. AI researchers
have devised a number of tools to solve these problems using methods from [probability](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]") theory and
economics.[[90]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
Precise mathematical tools have been developed that analyse how an agent can make
choices and plan, using [decision theory](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color"), [decision analysis](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color"),[[91]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
and [information value theory](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "
title=").[[92]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
These tools include models such as [Markov decision processes](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "
title="),[[93]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
dynamic [decision networks](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence "
title="),[[94]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options")
[game theory](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options") and [mechanism design](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User
menu").[[95]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")

[Bayesian networks](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User
menu")[[96]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
are a tool that can be used for [reasoning](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=") (using the [Bayesian inference](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
algorithm),[[i]](# "Contents")[[98]](# "Contents") [learning](# "Contents") (using the [expectation–maximisation algorithm](#
"Contents")),[[j]](#Goals "Contents")[[100]](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents")
[planning](#Knowledge_representation "Contents") (using [decision networks](#Knowledge_representation
"Contents"))[[101]](#Planning_and_decision-making "Contents") and [perception](#Learning "Contents") (using [dynamic Bayesian networks](#Learning
"Contents")).[[94]](#Natural_language_processing "Contents")

Probabilistic algorithms can also be used for filtering, prediction, smoothing, and
finding explanations for streams of data, thus helping perception systems analyse
processes that occur over time (e.g., [hidden Markov models](#Perception "Contents") or [Kalman filters](#Social_intelligence
"Contents")).[[94]](#General_intelligence "Contents")
[![vector-toc-list-item vector-toc-level-2](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Techniques "Contents")
[Expectation–maximisation](#State_space_search "Contents") [clustering](#State_space_search "Contents") of [Old Faithful](#State_space_search "Contents") eruption data starts from a random guess but then successfully converges on an accurate clustering of the two physically distinct modes of eruption.


### Classifiers and statistical learning methods

The simplest AI applications can be divided into two types: classifiers (e.g., "if
shiny then diamond"), on one hand, and controllers (e.g., "if diamond then pick up"),
on the other hand. [Classifiers](#Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning "Contents")[[102]](#Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods "Contents")
are functions that use [pattern matching](#Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods "Contents") to determine the closest match. They can be fine-tuned based on chosen examples using [supervised learning](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents"). Each pattern (also called an "[observation](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents")") is labeled with a certain predefined class. All the observations combined with their class labels are known as a [data set](#Deep_learning "Contents"). When a new observation is received, that observation is classified based on previous
experience.[[47]](#GPT "Contents")

There are many kinds of classifiers in use.[[103]](#Hardware_and_software "Contents")
The [decision tree](#Applications "Contents") is the simplest and most widely used symbolic machine learning
algorithm.[[104]](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") [K-nearest neighbour](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") algorithm was the most widely used analogical AI until the mid-1990s, and [Kernel methods](#Chatbots "Contents") such as the [support vector machine](#Chatbots "Contents") (SVM) displaced k-nearest neighbour in the
1990s.[[105]](#Physical_AI "Contents")The [naive Bayes classifier](#Health_and_medicine "Contents") is reportedly the "most widely used
learner"[[106]](#Finance "Contents") at Google, due in part to its scalability.[[107]](#Military "Contents")[Neural networks](#Generative_AI "Contents") are also used as
classifiers.[[108]](#Agents "Contents")


### Artificial neural networks
[![Tuigse inntealta – Scottish Gaelic](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Web_search "Contents")
A neural network is an interconnected group of nodes, akin to the vast network of
[neurons](#Ethics "Contents") in the [human brain](#Ethics "Contents").
An artificial neural network is based on a collection of nodes also known as [artificial neurons](#Risks_and_harm "Contents"), which loosely model the [neurons](#Risks_and_harm "Contents") in a biological brain. It is trained to recognise patterns; once trained, it can recognise those patterns in fresh data. There is an input, at least one hidden layer of nodes and an output. Each node applies a function and once the [weight](#Privacy_and_copyright "Contents") crosses its specified threshold, the data is transmitted to the next layer. A network is typically called a deep neural network if it has at least 2 hidden
layers.[[108]](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents")

Learning algorithms for neural networks use [local search](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents") to choose the weights that will get the right output for each input during training. The most common training technique is the [backpropagation](#Misinformation "Contents")
algorithm.[[109]](#Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness "Contents") Neural networks learn
to model complex relationships between inputs and outputs and [find patterns](#Lack_of_transparency "Contents") in data. In theory, a neural network can learn any
function.[[110]](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents")

In [feedforward neural networks](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents") the signal passes in only one
direction.[[111]](#Technological_unemployment "Contents") The term [perceptron](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents") typically refers to a single-layer neural
network.[[112]](#Existential_risk "Contents") In contrast, deep learning uses many
layers.[[113]](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents") [Recurrent neural networks](#Open_source "Contents") (RNNs) feed the output signal back into the input, which allows short-term memories of previous input events. [Long short-term memory](#Open_source "Contents") networks (LSTMs) are recurrent neural networks that better preserve longterm dependencies and are less sensitive to the [vanishing gradient problem](#Frameworks
"Contents").[[114]](#Regulation "Contents") [Convolutional neural networks](#History "Contents") (CNNs) use layers of [kernels](#Philosophy "Contents") to more efficiently process local patterns. This local processing is especially important in [image processing](#Philosophy "Contents"), where the early CNN layers typically identify simple local patterns such as edges and curves, with subsequent layers detecting more complex patterns like textures, and eventually whole
objects.[[115]](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents")


### Deep learning
[![Tuigse inntealta – Scottish Gaelic](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Legal_definitions "Contents")
[Deep learning](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits "Contents") is a subset of [machine learning](#Neat_vs._scruffy "Contents"), which is itself a subset of artificial
intelligence.[[116]](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents")
[Deep learning](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents") uses several layers of neurons between the network's inputs and
outputs.[[113]](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents") The multiple
layers can progressively extract higher-level features from the raw input. For example,
in [image processing](#Consciousness "Contents"), lower layers may identify edges, while higher layers may identify the concepts relevant to a human such as digits, letters, or
faces.[[117]](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents")

Deep learning has profoundly improved the performance of programs in many important
subfields of artificial intelligence, including [computer vision](#Future "Contents"), [speech recognition](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents"), [natural language processing](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents"), [image classification](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity
"Contents"),[[118]](#In_fiction "Contents") and others. The reason that deep learning
performs so well in so many applications is not known as of 2021.[[119]](#Further_reading "Contents")
The sudden success of deep learning in 2012–2015 did not occur because of some
new discovery or theoretical breakthrough (deep neural networks and backpropagation
had been described by many people, as far back as the 1950s)[[k]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown vector-page-titlebar-toc vector-button-flush-left")
but because of two factors: the increase in [computer power](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown-checkbox ") (including the hundred-fold increase in speed by switching to [GPUs](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown-label cdx-button cdx-button--fake-button cdx-button--fake-button--enabled cdx-button--weight-quiet cdx-button--icon-only ")) and the availability of vast amounts of training data, especially the giant [curated datasets](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-unpinned-container") used for benchmark testing, such as [ImageNet](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie
"vector-unpinned-container").[[l]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans")


### GPT

[Generative pre-trained transformers](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans") (GPTs) are [large language models](https://als.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%BCnstliche_Intelligenz "Kunsmatige intelligensie") (LLMs) that generate text based on the semantic relationships between words in sentences. Text-based GPT models are pre-trained on a large [corpus of text](gsw "Künstliche Intelligenz – Alemannic") that can be from the Internet. The pretraining consists of predicting the next [token](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%88%B0%E1%8B%8D_%E1%88%A0%E1%88%AB%E1%88%BD_%E1%8B%A8%E1%88%9B%E1%88%B0%E1%89%A5_%E1%89%BD%E1%88%8E%E1%89%B3 "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic") (a token being usually a word, subword, or punctuation). Throughout this pretraining, GPT models accumulate knowledge about the world and can then generate human-like text by repeatedly predicting the next token. Typically, a subsequent training phase makes the model more truthful, useful, and harmless, usually with a technique called [reinforcement learning from human feedback](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelichencia_artificial "Intelichencia artificial – Aragonese") (RLHF). Current GPT models are prone to generating falsehoods called "hallucinations". These can be reduced with RLHF and quality data, but the problem has been getting worse for reasoning
systems.[[127]](anp "कृत्रिम बुद्धि") Such systems are
used in [chatbots](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic"), which allow people to ask a question or request a task in simple
text.[[128]](https://arz.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%89 "ذكاء صناعى – Egyptian
Arabic")[[129]](https://as.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A7%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE_%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese")

Current models and services include [ChatGPT](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese"), [Claude](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা"), [Gemini](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelixencia_artificial "Intelixencia artificial – Asturian"), [Copilot](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelixencia_artificial "Intelixencia artificial – Asturian"), and [Meta AI](ast "Intelixencia
artificial").[[130]](az "Süni intellekt") [Multimodal](https://azb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D9%85%D8%B5%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B9%DB%8C_%D8%B0%DA%A9%D8%A7 "مصنوعی ذکا – South Azerbaijani") GPT models can process different types of data ([modalities](azb "مصنوعی ذکا – South Azerbaijani")) such as images, videos, sound, and
text.[[131]](bar "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz")


### Hardware and software

predominant.[[134]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

The transistor density in [integrated circuits](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") has been observed to roughly double every 18 months—a trend known as [Moore's law](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), named after the [Intel](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") co-founder [Gordon Moore](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), who first identified it. Improvements in [GPUs](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") have been even
faster,[[135]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
a trend sometimes called [Huang's law](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia"),[[136]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
named after [Nvidia](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") co-founder and CEO [Jensen Huang](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia").


## Applications

Main article: [Applications of artificial intelligence](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
[AI Overviews](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), an example of AI use on search engines
AI and machine learning technology is used in most of the essential applications
of the 2020s, including:

- [search engines](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (such as [Google Search](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"))
- [targeting online advertisements](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
- [recommendation systems](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") (offered by [Netflix](//upload.wikimedia.org "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), [YouTube](//upload.wikimedia.org "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") or [Amazon](//upload.wikimedia.org "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")) driving [internet traffic](//upload.wikimedia.org "Wikipedia (en)")
- [targeted advertising](/static/favicon/wikipedia.ico "Wikipedia (en)") ([AdSense](//en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=rsd "Wikipedia Atom feed"), [Facebook](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.en "Wikipedia Atom feed"))
- [virtual assistants](/w/index.php?title=Special:RecentChanges&feed=atom "Wikipedia Atom feed") (such as [Siri](//meta.wikimedia.org "></script></head>
<body class=") or [Alexa](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="))
- [autonomous vehicles](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") (including [drones](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="), [ADAS](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") and [self-driving cars](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="))
- [automatic language translation](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") ([Microsoft Translator](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="), [Google Translate](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="))
- [facial recognition](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") ([Apple](#bodyContent "Main menu")'s [FaceID](#bodyContent "Main menu") or [Facebook](#bodyContent "Main menu")'s [DeepFace](#bodyContent "Main menu") and [Google](#bodyContent "Main menu")'s [FaceNet](#bodyContent "Main menu"))
- [image labelling](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu") (used by Facebook, Apple's [Photos](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu") and [TikTok](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu")).

The deployment of AI may be overseen by a [chief automation officer](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") (CAO).
