### Health and medicine

Main article: [Artificial intelligence in healthcare](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
[AlphaFold 2](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]") (2021) demonstrated the ability to approximate, in hours rather than months, the 3D [structure of a protein](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia
[f]").[[137]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
In 2023, it was reported that AI-guided drug discovery helped find a class of antibiotics
capable of killing two different types of drug-resistant bacteria.[[138]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
In 2024, researchers used machine learning to accelerate the search for [Parkinson's disease](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color") drug treatments. Their aim was to identify compounds that block the clumping, or aggregation, of [alpha-synuclein](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") (the protein that characterises Parkinson's disease). They were able to speed up the initial screening process ten-fold and reduce the cost by a
thousand-fold.[[139]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "
title=")[[140]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")

AI is increasingly being used in medical diagnostics, including the detection of
diseases such as lung cancer from medical imaging like [CT scans](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=").
[[141]](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")

A 2026 *[Nature](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "You're encouraged to log in; however, it's not mandatory. [o]")*
article titled "Dozens of AI disease-prediction models were trained on dubious data"
highlighted the use of unreliable data being used to train AI medical prediction
models for [stroke](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options") and [diabetes](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") in 125 research articles. Evidence suggested some of the AI tools that were developed on unreliable data had been used on patients, although it was not clear if there were adverse
outcomes.[[142]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User
menu")[[143]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")


### Gaming

Main article: [Artificial intelligence in video games](# "Contents")
[Game playing](# "Contents") programs have been used since the 1950s to demonstrate and test AI's most advanced
techniques.[[144]](# "Contents") [Deep Blue](# "Contents") became the first computer chess-playing system to beat a reigning world chess champion, [Garry Kasparov](# "Contents"), on 11 May
1997.[[145]](# "Contents") In 2011, in a *[Jeopardy!](# "Contents")* [quiz show](#Goals "Contents") exhibition match, [IBM](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents")'s [question answering system](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents"), [Watson](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents"), defeated the two greatest
*Jeopardy!* champions, [Brad Rutter](#Knowledge_representation "Contents") and [Ken Jennings](#Knowledge_representation "Contents"), by a significant
margin.[[146]](#Planning_and_decision-making "Contents") In March 2016, [AlphaGo](#Planning_and_decision-making "Contents") won 4 out of 5 games of [Go](#Learning "Contents") in a match with Go champion [Lee Sedol](#Learning "Contents"), becoming the first [computer Go](#Learning "Contents")-playing system to beat a professional Go player without [handicaps](#Natural_language_processing "Contents"). Then, in 2017, it [defeated Ke Jie](#Natural_language_processing "Contents"), who was the best Go player in the
world.[[147]](#Perception "Contents") Other programs handle [imperfect-information](#Social_intelligence "Contents") games, such as the [poker](#General_intelligence "Contents")-playing program [Pluribus](#General_intelligence
"Contents").[[148]](#Techniques "Contents") [DeepMind](#Techniques "Contents") developed increasingly generalistic [reinforcement learning](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents") models, such as with [MuZero](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents"), which could be trained to play chess, Go, or [Atari](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents")
games.[[149]](#State_space_search "Contents") In 2019, DeepMind's AlphaStar achieved
grandmaster level in [StarCraft II](#Local_search "Contents"), a particularly challenging real-time strategy game that involves incomplete knowledge of what happens on the
map.[[150]](#Logic "Contents") In 2021, an AI agent competed in a PlayStation [Gran Turismo](#Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning "Contents") competition, winning against four of the world's best Gran Turismo drivers using deep reinforcement
learning.[[151]](#Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods "Contents") In 2024,
Google DeepMind introduced SIMA, a type of AI capable of autonomously playing nine
previously unseen [open-world](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents") video games by observing screen output, as well as executing short, specific tasks in response to natural language
instructions.[[152]](#Deep_learning "Contents")


### Mathematics

See also: [AlphaDev](#Applications "Contents")
In mathematics, probabilistic large language models are versatile, but can also produce
wrong answers in the form of [hallucinations](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents"). The [Alibaba Group](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") developed a version of its *[Qwen](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents")*
models called *Qwen2-Math*, that achieved state-of-the-art performance on several
mathematical benchmarks, including 84% accuracy on the MATH dataset of competition
mathematics problems.[[153]](#Physical_AI "Contents") In January 2025, Microsoft
proposed the technique *rStar-Math* that leverages [Monte Carlo tree search](#Health_and_medicine "Contents") and step-by-step reasoning, enabling a relatively small language model like
*Qwen-7B* to solve 53% of the [AIME](#Gaming "Contents") 2024 and 90% of the MATH benchmark
problems.[[154]](#Mathematics "Contents") [Google DeepMind](#Finance "Contents") has developed models for solving mathematical problems: *[AlphaTensor](#Finance
"Contents")*, *[AlphaGeometry](#Military "Contents")*, *AlphaProof*, *[AlphaEvolve](#Military "Contents"), and [FunSearch](#Military
"Contents").*[[155]](#Agents "Contents")[[156]](#Web_search "Contents")

When natural language is used to describe mathematical problems, converters can transform
such prompts into a formal language such as [Lean](#Sexuality "Contents") to define mathematical tasks. The experimental model
*Gemini Deep Think* accepts natural language prompts directly and achieved gold
medal results in the [International Math Olympiad](#Other_industry-specific_tasks "Contents") of
2025.[[157]](#Ethics "Contents")

[Topological deep learning](#Risks_and_harm "Contents") integrates various [topological](#Risks_and_harm "Contents") approaches.


### Finance

According to Nicolas Firzli, director of the [World Pensions & Investments Forum](#Risks_and_harm "Contents"), it may be too early to see the emergence of highly innovative AI-informed financial products and services. He argues that "the deployment of AI tools will simply further automatise things: destroying tens of thousands of jobs in banking, financial planning, and pension advice in the process, but I'm not sure it will unleash a new wave of [e.g., sophisticated] pension
innovation."[[158]](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents")


### Military

Main article: [Military applications of artificial intelligence](#Lack_of_transparency "Contents")
Various countries are deploying AI military applications.[[159]](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents")
The main applications enhance [command and control](#Technological_unemployment "Contents"), communications, sensors, integration and
interoperability.[[160]](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents")
Research is targeting intelligence collection and analysis, logistics, cyber operations,
information operations, and semiautonomous and [autonomous vehicles](#Existential_risk
"Contents").[[159]](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents") AI technologies
enable coordination of sensors and effectors, threat detection and identification,
marking of enemy positions, [target acquisition](#Open_source "Contents"), coordination and deconfliction of distributed [Joint Fires](#Open_source "Contents") between networked combat vehicles, both human-operated and
autonomous.[[160]](#Frameworks "Contents")

AI has been used in military operations in Iraq, Syria, Israel and Ukraine.[[159]](#History
"Contents")[[161]](#Philosophy "Contents")[[162]](#Defining_artificial_intelligence
"Contents")[[163]](#Legal_definitions "Contents")


### Generative AI

These paragraphs are an excerpt from [Generative AI](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents").[[edit](#Narrow_vs._general_AI
"Contents")]


[Generative artificial intelligence](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents") (GenAI) is a subfield of artificial intelligence (AI) that uses [generative models](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents") to generate text, [images](#Consciousness "Contents"), [videos](#Consciousness "Contents"), [audio](#Consciousness "Contents"), [software code](#Consciousness "Contents") or other forms of
data.[[164]](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents") These models [learn the underlying patterns](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents") and structures of their [training data](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents"), and use them to generate new
data[[165]](#Future "Contents") in response to input, which often takes the form
of [natural language](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents") [prompts](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity
"Contents").[[166]](#Transhumanism "Contents")[[167]](#See_also "Contents")

The prevalence of generative AI tools has increased significantly since the [AI boom](#Explanatory_notes "Contents") in the 2020s. This boom was made possible by improvements in [deep](#Explanatory_notes "Contents") [neural networks](#Explanatory_notes "Contents"), particularly [large language models](#References "Contents") (LLMs), which are based on the [transformer](#References "Contents") architecture. Generative AI [applications](#Further_reading "Contents") include [chatbots](#Further_reading "Contents") such as [ChatGPT](#Textbooks "Contents"), [Claude](#Textbooks "Contents"), [Microsoft Copilot](#Textbooks "Contents"), [DeepSeek](#Textbooks "Contents"), [Doubao](#History_of_AI "Contents"), [Google Gemini](#History_of_AI "Contents"), [Grok](#History_of_AI "Contents"), [Kimi](#Other_sources "Contents") and [Qwen](#Other_sources "Contents"); [text-to-image](#Other_sources "Contents") models such as [DALL-E](#Other_sources "Contents"), [Firefly](#External_links "Contents"), [Stable Diffusion](#External_links "Contents"), and [Midjourney](#External_links "Contents"); and [text-to-video](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents") models such as [Veo](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents"), [LTX](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents") and [Sora](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown vector-page-titlebar-toc
vector-button-flush-left").[[168]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie
"vector-page-titlebar-toc-checkbox")[[169]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie
"vector-unpinned-container")[[170]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans")

Companies in a variety of sectors have used generative AI, including those in software
development, healthcare,[[171]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans")
finance,[[172]](https://als.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%BCnstliche_Intelligenz "Künstliche Intelligenz – Alemannic")
entertainment,[[173]](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%88%B0%E1%8B%8D_%E1%88%A0%E1%88%AB%E1%88%BD_%E1%8B%A8%E1%88%9B%E1%88%B0%E1%89%A5_%E1%89%BD%E1%88%8E%E1%89%B3 "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic")
customer service,[[174]](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelichencia_artificial "Intelichencia artificial – Aragonese")
sales and marketing,[[175]](anp "कृत्रिम बुद्धि – Angika")
art, writing,[[176]](ar "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic") and product design.[[177]](ary "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan Arabic")


### Agents

Main article: [Agentic AI](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelixencia_artificial "Intelixencia artificial – Asturian")

See also: [OpenClaw](azb "مصنوعی ذکا – South Azerbaijani") and [CrewAI](https://ba.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%AF%D2%BB%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BC%D0%B0_%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "مصنوعی ذکا")
AI agents are software entities designed to perceive their environment, make decisions,
and take actions autonomously to achieve specific goals. These agents can interact
with users, their environment, or other agents. AI agents are used in various applications,
including [virtual assistants](ba "Яһалма интеллект"), [chatbots](https://bar.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinschtlicha_Intelligenz "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz – Bavarian"), [autonomous vehicles](https://bar.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinschtlicha_Intelligenz "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz – Bavarian"), [game-playing systems](bar "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz"), and [industrial robotics](https://bat-smg.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%97rbt%C4%97ns_intelekts "Dėrbtėns intelekts – Samogitian"). AI agents operate within the constraints of their programming, available computational resources, and hardware limitations. This means they are restricted to performing tasks within their defined scope and have finite memory and processing capabilities. In real-world applications, AI agents often face time constraints for decision-making and action execution. Many AI agents incorporate learning algorithms, enabling them to improve their performance over time through experience or training. Using machine learning, AI agents can adapt to new situations and optimise their behaviour for their designated
tasks.[[178]](be-tarask "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian (Taraškievica
orthography)")[[179]](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B_%D1%96%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%8D%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Штучны інтэлект –
Belarusian")[[180]](https://bew.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calakan_bikinan "Calakan bikinan – Betawi")

that analyse user data to offer predictions,[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

## Ethics

Main article: [Ethics of artificial intelligence](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")[![](/static/images/icons/enwiki-25.svg "Articles related to current events")](/wiki/Portal:Current_events "Guides to browsing Wikipedia")
[Street art in Tel Aviv](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia")[[199]](/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "The hub for
editors")[[200]](/wiki/Special:SpecialPages "Add images or other media for use on Wikipedia")
AI has potential benefits and potential risks.[[201]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")
AI may be able to advance science and find solutions for serious problems: [Demis Hassabis](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]") of [DeepMind](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]") hopes to "solve intelligence, and then use that to solve everything
else".[[202]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
However, as the use of AI has become widespread, several unintended consequences
and risks have been identified.[[203]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color")[[204]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
In-production systems can sometimes not factor ethics and bias into their AI training
processes, especially when the AI algorithms are inherently unexplainable in deep
learning.[[205]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")


### Risks and harm


#### Privacy and copyright

Further information: [Information privacy](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") and [Artificial intelligence and copyright](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")
Machine learning algorithms require large amounts of data. The techniques used to
acquire this data have raised concerns about [privacy](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title="), [surveillance](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") and [copyright](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=").

AI-powered devices and services, such as virtual assistants and IoT products, continuously
collect personal information, raising concerns about intrusive data gathering and
unauthorised access by third parties. The loss of privacy is further exacerbated
by AI's ability to process and combine vast amounts of data, potentially leading
to a surveillance society where individual activities are constantly monitored and
analysed without adequate safeguards or transparency.

Sensitive user data collected may include online activity records, geolocation data,
video, or audio.[[206]](# "Contents") For example, in order to build [speech recognition](# "Contents") algorithms, [Amazon](# "Contents") has recorded millions of private conversations and allowed [temporary workers](# "Contents") to listen to and transcribe some of
them.[[207]](#Goals "Contents") Opinions about this widespread surveillance range
from those who see it as a [necessary evil](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents") to those for whom it is clearly [unethical](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents") and a violation of the [right to privacy](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving
"Contents").[[208]](#Planning_and_decision-making "Contents")

AI developers argue that this is the only way to deliver valuable applications and
have developed several techniques that attempt to preserve privacy while still obtaining
the data, such as [data aggregation](#Natural_language_processing "Contents"), [de-identification](#Natural_language_processing "Contents") and [differential privacy](#Natural_language_processing
"Contents").[[209]](#General_intelligence "Contents") Since 2016, some privacy experts,
such as [Cynthia Dwork](#Techniques "Contents"), have begun to view privacy in terms of [fairness](#Techniques "Contents"). [Brian Christian](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents") wrote that experts have pivoted "from the question of 'what they know' to the question of 'what they're doing with
it'."[[210]](#Local_search "Contents")

Generative AI is often trained on unlicensed copyrighted works, including in domains
such as images or computer code; the output is then used under the rationale of "[fair use](#Logic "Contents")". Experts disagree about how well and under what circumstances this rationale will hold up in courts of law; relevant factors may include "the purpose and character of the use of the copyrighted work" and "the effect upon the potential market for the copyrighted
work".[[211]](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents")[[212]](#Deep_learning "Contents")
Website owners can indicate that they do not want their content scraped via a "[robots.txt](#Deep_learning "Contents")"
file.[[213]](#GPT "Contents") However, some companies will scrape content regardless[[214]](#Applications
"Contents")[[215]](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") because the robots.txt
file has no real authority. In 2023, leading authors (including [John Grisham](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") and [Jonathan Franzen](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents")) sued AI companies for using their work to train generative
AI.[[216]](#Health_and_medicine "Contents")[[217]](#Finance "Contents") Another
discussed approach is to envision a separate *[sui generis](#Finance "Contents")*
system of protection for creations generated by AI to ensure fair attribution and
compensation for human authors.[[218]](#Generative_AI "Contents")


#### Dominance by tech giants

The commercial AI scene is dominated by [Big Tech](#Agents "Contents") companies such as [Alphabet Inc.](#Web_search "Contents"), [Amazon](#Web_search "Contents"), [Apple Inc.](#Web_search "Contents"), [Meta Platforms](#Sexuality "Contents"), and [Microsoft](#Sexuality
"Contents").[[219]](#Other_industry-specific_tasks "Contents")[[220]](#Ethics "Contents")[[221]](#Risks_and_harm "Contents")
Some of these players already own the vast majority of existing [cloud infrastructure](#Privacy_and_copyright "Contents") and [computing](#Privacy_and_copyright "Contents") power from [data centres](#Privacy_and_copyright "Contents"), allowing them to entrench further in the
marketplace.[[222]](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents")[[223]](#Misinformation "Contents")

For most of 2025-2026, AI-related companies have dominated stock market returns.
Recently, investors have started questioning whether the enormous spending on AI
infrastructure and data centers will generate sufficient profits, leading to increased
volatility in technology and semiconductor stocks. [[224]](#Lack_of_transparency "Contents")


#### Power needs and environmental impacts

See also: [Environmental impacts of artificial intelligence](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents") and [AI build-out financing](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents")[![Tuigse inntealta – Scottish Gaelic](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/1b/Semi-protection-shackle.svg/20px-Semi-protection-shackle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Existential_risk "Contents")
Fuelled by a growth in AI, data centres' demand for power increased in the 2020s.[[225]](#Frameworks "Contents")
Technology companies have built electricity and artificial intelligence infrastructure
to facilitate the AI boom of the 2020s. A 2025 report from the consulting firm [McKinsey & Company](#History "Contents") estimated that by 2030, $2.7 trillion would be invested into AI infrastructure and data centres in the US, surpassing World War II's [Manhattan Project](#History "Contents") every
month.[[226]](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents")

In January 2024, the [International Energy Agency](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents") (IEA) released
*Electricity 2024, Analysis and Forecast to 2026*.[[227]](#Legal_definitions "Contents")
This is the first IEA report to make projections for data centres and power consumption
by AI and cryptocurrency. The report states that power demand for these uses might
double by 2026, with the additional power consumption equaling that of Japan.[[228]](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits "Contents")

Power consumption by AI is responsible for an increase in fossil fuel use, and has
delayed closings of obsolete, carbon-emitting coal energy facilities. A ChatGPT search
involves 10 times as much electrical energy as a Google search.[[229]](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents")

A 2024 [Goldman Sachs](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents") research paper, *AI Data
Centers and the Coming US Power Demand Surge*, found "US power demand (is) likely
to experience growth not seen in a generation...." and forecasts that, by 2030, US
data centres will consume 8% of US power, as opposed to 3% in 2022, presaging growth
for the electrical power generation industry by a variety of means.[[230]](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents")
Data centres' need for more and more electrical power is such that they might max
out the electrical grid. The Big Tech companies counter that AI can be used to maximise
the utilisation of the grid by all.[[231]](#Computationalism_and_functionalism "Contents")

In 2024, *The Wall Street Journal* reported that big AI companies have begun negotiations
with the US nuclear power providers to provide electricity to the data centres. In
March 2024, Amazon purchased a Pennsylvania nuclear-powered data centre for US$650
million.[[232]](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents")

In September 2024, [Microsoft](#Future "Contents") announced an agreement with [Constellation Energy](#Future "Contents") to re-open the [Three Mile Island](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents") nuclear power plant to provide Microsoft with 100% of all electric power produced by the plant for 20 years. Reopening the plant, which suffered a partial nuclear meltdown of its Unit 2 reactor in 1979, will require Constellation to get through strict regulatory processes which will include extensive safety scrutiny from the US [Nuclear Regulatory Commission](#Transhumanism "Contents"). If approved (this will be the first ever US re-commissioning of a nuclear plant), over 835 megawatts of power – enough for 800,000 homes – will be produced. The cost for re-opening and upgrading is estimated at US$1.6 billion and is dependent on tax breaks for nuclear power contained in the 2022 US [Inflation Reduction Act](#In_fiction
"Contents").[[233]](#See_also "Contents") As of 2024, the US government and the
state of Michigan have been investing almost US$2 billion to reopen the [Palisades nuclear reactor](#Explanatory_notes "Contents") on Lake Michigan. Closed since 2022, the plant was scheduled to be reopened in October
2025.[[234]](#References "Contents")

After the last approval in September 2023, [Taiwan](#Further_reading "Contents") suspended the approval of data centres north of [Taoyuan](#Textbooks "Contents") with a capacity of more than 5 MW in 2024, due to power supply
shortages.[[235]](#History_of_AI "Contents") Taiwan aims to [phase out nuclear power](#History_of_AI "Contents") by
2025.[[235]](#Other_sources "Contents")

[Singapore](#External_links "Contents") imposed a ban on the opening of data centres in 2019 due to electric power, but lifted it in
2022.[[235]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Contents")

Although most nuclear plants in Japan have been shut down after the 2011 [Fukushima nuclear accident](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Table of Contents"), according to an October 2024
*Bloomberg* article in Japanese, cloud gaming services company Ubitus, in which
Nvidia has a stake, is looking for land in Japan near a nuclear power plant for a
new data centre for generative AI.[[236]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-unpinned-container")

On 1 November 2024, the [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "p-lang-btn") (FERC) rejected an application submitted by [Talen Energy](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans") for approval to supply some electricity from the nuclear power station [Susquehanna](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans") to Amazon's data
centre.[[237]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie –
Afrikaans")According to the Commission Chairman [Willie L. Phillips](af "Kunsmatige intelligensie"), it is a burden on the electricity grid as well as a significant cost-shifting concern to households and other business
sectors.[[237]](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%88%B0%E1%8B%8D_%E1%88%A0%E1%88%AB%E1%88%BD_%E1%8B%A8%E1%88%9B%E1%88%B0%E1%89%A5_%E1%89%BD%E1%88%8E%E1%89%B3 "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic")

In 2025, a report prepared by the IEA estimated the [greenhouse gas emissions](am "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic") from the energy consumption of AI at 180 million tons. By 2035, these emissions could rise to 300–500 million tonnes depending on what measures will be taken. This is below 1.5% of the energy sector emissions. The emissions reduction potential of AI was estimated at 5% of the energy sector emissions, but [rebound effects](an "Intelichencia artificial") (for example if people switch from public transport to autonomous cars) can reduce
it.[[238]](anp "कृत्रिम बुद्धि")

In June 2026, the [United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic") released a report about cumulative environmental impacts of AI, not only carbon. The report found that AI has significant negative impacts on land, water, and climate, as it uses large amounts of electricity, requires [mining](ary "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan Arabic") of [minerals](ary "دكا صطيناعي"), and generates large amounts of [electronic waste](https://arz.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%89 "ذكاء صناعى – Egyptian Arabic"). In 2025, data centres consumed more electricity than Saudi Arabia, and ChatGPT alone consumed an amount of water equivalent to the needs of 500,000 people in Sub-Saharan Africa. The negative impacts are not distributed equally across the planet but are concentrated in some places. Data centres are often built in places already suffering from water deficit. For example, AI deployment has already led to an increase in [water scarcity](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese") in Mexico and Uruguay. It created problems with energy supply in Ireland, which forbade construction of new data centres near Dublin until 2028. Measures can involve tradeoffs, for example, transitioning from coal to [bioenergy](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelixencia_artificial "Intelixencia artificial – Asturian") reduces carbon footprint but increases the impact on land and water. Energy efficiency might not reduce environmental impact, because as AI becomes more efficient, it also becomes cheaper and more widely
used.[[11]](az "Süni intellekt – Azerbaijani")


#### Misinformation

See also: [Content moderation](https://bar.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinschtlicha_Intelligenz "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz – Bavarian")
[YouTube](bar "Kinschtlicha Intelligenz"), [Facebook](https://bat-smg.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%97rbt%C4%97ns_intelekts "Dėrbtėns intelekts – Samogitian") and others use [recommender systems](https://bat-smg.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%97rbt%C4%97ns_intelekts "Dėrbtėns intelekts – Samogitian") to guide users to more content. These AI programs were given the goal of [maximising](https://bcl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artipisyal_na_intelihensya "Dėrbtėns intelekts") user engagement (that is, the only goal was to keep people watching). The AI learned that users tended to choose [misinformation](bcl "Artipisyal na intelihensya – Central Bikol"), [conspiracy theories](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B_%D1%96%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%8D%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Artipisyal na intelihensya"), and extreme [partisan](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B_%D1%96%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%8D%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)") content, and, to keep them watching, the AI recommended more of it. Users also tended to watch more content on the same subject, so the AI led people into [filter bubbles](be-tarask "Штучны інтэлект") where they received multiple versions of the same
misinformation.[[239]](bew "Calakan bikinan – Betawi") This convinced many users
that the misinformation was true, and ultimately undermined trust in institutions,
the media and the government.[[240]](https://bh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9F%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AB%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B2_%E0%A4%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%B8 "आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस – Bhojpuri")
The AI program had correctly learned to maximise its goal, but the result was harmful
to society. After the U.S. election in 2016, major technology companies took some
steps to mitigate the problem.[[241]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")

In the early 2020s, [generative AI](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") began to create images, audio, and texts that are virtually indistinguishable from real photographs, recordings, or human
writing,[[242]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
while realistic AI-generated videos became feasible in the mid-2020s.[[243]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")[[244]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia")[[245]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
It is possible for bad actors to use this technology to create massive amounts of
misinformation and [computational propaganda](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") through techniques such as
deepfakes.[[246]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia")[[247]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
AI pioneer and Nobel Prize-winning computer scientist [Geoffrey Hinton](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") expressed concern about AI enabling "authoritarian leaders to manipulate their electorates" on a large scale, among other
risks.[[248]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
The ability to influence electorates has been proved in at least one study. This
same study shows more inaccurate statements from the models when they advocate for
candidates of the political right.[[249]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

AI researchers at [Microsoft](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), [OpenAI](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia"), universities and other organisations have suggested using "[personhood credentials](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")" as a way to overcome online deception enabled by AI
models.[[250]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")


#### Algorithmic bias and fairness

Main articles: [Algorithmic bias](/static/apple-touch/wikipedia.png "Wikipedia (en)") and [Fairness (machine learning)](/w/rest.php/v1/search "Wikipedia (en)")
Machine learning applications can be [biased](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Wikipedia Atom
feed")[[m]](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") if they learn from biased data.[[252]](#bodyContent "Main menu") The
developers may not be aware that the bias exists.[[253]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
Discriminatory behaviour by some LLMs can be observed in their output.[[254]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
Bias can be introduced by the way [training data](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") is selected and by the way a model is
deployed.[[255]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")[[252]](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us "How to contact Wikipedia")
If a biased algorithm is used to make decisions that can seriously [harm](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia") people (as it can in [medicine](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia"), [finance](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia"), [recruitment](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Learn how to edit Wikipedia"), [housing](/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "The hub for editors") or [policing](/wiki/Special:RecentChanges "A list of recent changes to Wikipedia [r]")) then the algorithm may cause [discrimination](/wiki/Wikipedia:File_upload_wizard "Add images or other media for use on
Wikipedia").[[256]](/wiki/Main_Page "Search Wikipedia [f]") The field of [fairness](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]") studies how to prevent harms from algorithmic biases.

On 28 June 2015, [Google Photos](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")'s new image labelling feature mistakenly identified Jacky Alcine and a friend as "gorillas" because they were black. The system was trained on a dataset that contained very few images of black
people,[[257]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
a problem called "sample size disparity".[[258]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
Google "fixed" this problem by preventing the system from labelling *anything* as
a "gorilla". Eight years later, in 2023, Google Photos still could not identify a
gorilla, and neither could similar products from Apple, Facebook, Microsoft and Amazon.[[259]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")

[COMPAS](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") is a commercial program widely used by [U.S. courts](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") to assess the likelihood of a [defendant](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=") becoming a [recidivist](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title="). In 2016, [Julia Angwin](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence "You are encouraged to create an account and log in; however, it is not mandatory") at [ProPublica](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=") discovered that COMPAS exhibited racial bias, despite the fact that the program was not told the races of the defendants. Although the error rate for both whites and blacks was calibrated equal at exactly 61%, the errors for each race were different—the system consistently overestimated the chance that a black person would re-offend and would underestimate the chance that a white person would not
re-offend.[[260]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")
In 2017, several researchers[[n]](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
showed that it was mathematically impossible for COMPAS to accommodate all possible
measures of fairness when the base rates of re-offence were different for whites
and blacks in the data.[[262]](# "Contents")

A program can make biased decisions even if the data does not explicitly mention
a problematic feature (such as "race" or "gender"). The feature will correlate with
other features (like "address", "shopping history" or "first name"), and the program
will make the same decisions based on these features as it would on "race" or "gender".[[263]](# "Contents")
Moritz Hardt said "the most robust fact in this research area is that fairness through
blindness doesn't work."[[264]](# "Contents")

Criticism of COMPAS highlighted that machine learning models are designed to make
"predictions" that are only valid if we assume that the future will resemble the
past. If they are trained on data that includes the results of racist decisions in
the past, machine learning models must predict that racist decisions will be made
in the future. If an application then uses these predictions as *recommendations*,
some of these "recommendations" will likely be racist.[[265]](#Knowledge_representation "Contents")
Thus, machine learning is not well suited to help make decisions in areas where there
is hope that the future will be *better* than the past. It is descriptive rather
than prescriptive.[[o]](#Natural_language_processing "Contents")

Bias and unfairness may go undetected because the developers are overwhelmingly white
and male: among AI engineers, about 4% are black and 20% are women.[[258]](#General_intelligence "Contents")

There are various conflicting definitions and mathematical models of fairness. These
notions depend on ethical assumptions, and are influenced by beliefs about society.
One broad category is [distributive fairness](#Techniques "Contents"), which focuses on the outcomes, often identifying groups and seeking to compensate for statistical disparities. Representational fairness tries to ensure that AI systems do not reinforce negative [stereotypes](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents") or render certain groups invisible. Procedural fairness focuses on the decision process rather than the outcome. The most relevant notions of fairness may depend on the context, notably the type of AI application and the stakeholders. The subjectivity in the notions of bias and fairness makes it difficult for companies to operationalise them. Having access to sensitive attributes such as race or gender is also considered by many AI ethicists to be necessary in order to compensate for biases, but it may conflict with [anti-discrimination laws](#State_space_search
"Contents").[[251]](#Logic "Contents")

At the 2022 [ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency](#Logic "Contents") a paper reported that a CLIP‑based ([Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training](#Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning "Contents")) robotic system reproduced harmful gender‑ and race‑linked stereotypes in a simulated manipulation task. The authors recommended robot‑learning methods which physically manifest such harms be "paused, reworked, or even wound down when appropriate, until outcomes can be proven safe, effective, and
just."[[267]](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents")[[268]](#Deep_learning "Contents")[[269]](#GPT "Contents")


#### Lack of transparency

See also: [Explainable AI](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents"), [Algorithmic transparency](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents"), and [Right to explanation](#Chatbots "Contents")
Many AI systems are so complex that their designers cannot explain how they reach
their decisions.[[270]](#Health_and_medicine "Contents") Particularly with [deep neural networks](#Gaming "Contents"), in which there are many non-[linear](#Mathematics "Contents") relationships between inputs and outputs. But some popular explainability techniques
exist.[[271]](#Finance "Contents")

It is impossible to be certain that a program is operating correctly if no one knows
how exactly it works. There have been many cases where a machine learning program
passed rigorous tests, but nevertheless learned something different than what the
programmers intended. For example, a system that could identify skin diseases better
than medical professionals was found to actually have a strong tendency to classify
images with a [ruler](#Generative_AI "Contents") as "cancerous", because pictures of malignancies typically include a ruler to show the
scale.[[272]](#Sexuality "Contents") Another machine learning system designed to
help effectively allocate medical resources was found to classify patients with asthma
as being at "low risk" of dying from pneumonia. Having asthma is actually a severe
risk factor, but since the patients having asthma would usually get much more medical
care, they were relatively unlikely to die according to the training data. The correlation
between asthma and low risk of dying from pneumonia was real, but misleading.[[273]](#Risks_and_harm "Contents")

People who have been harmed by an algorithm's decision have a right to an explanation.[[274]](#Dominance_by_tech_giants "Contents")
Doctors, for example, are expected to clearly and completely explain to their colleagues
the reasoning behind any decision they make. Early drafts of the European Union's
[General Data Protection Regulation](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents") in 2016 included an explicit statement that this right
exists.[[p]](#Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness "Contents") Industry experts noted that
this is an unsolved problem with no solution in sight. Regulators argued that nevertheless
the harm is real: if the problem has no solution, the tools should not be used.[[275]](#Technological_unemployment "Contents")

[DARPA](#Technological_unemployment "Contents") established the [XAI](#Substitution_for_human–human_interaction "Contents") ("Explainable Artificial Intelligence") program in 2014 to try to solve these
problems.[[276]](#Ethical_machines_and_alignment "Contents")

Several approaches aim to address the transparency problem. SHAP enables to visualise
the contribution of each feature to the output.[[277]](#Regulation "Contents") LIME
can locally approximate a model's outputs with a simpler, interpretable model.[[278]](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents")
[Multitask learning](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents") provides a large number of outputs in addition to the target classification. These other outputs can help developers deduce what the network has
learned.[[279]](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits "Contents") [Deconvolution](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits "Contents"), [DeepDream](#Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits "Contents") and other [generative](#Neat_vs._scruffy "Contents") methods can allow developers to see what different layers of a deep network for computer vision have learned, and produce output that can suggest what the network is
learning.[[280]](#Narrow_vs._general_AI "Contents") For [generative pre-trained transformers](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents"), [Anthropic](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents") developed a technique based on [dictionary learning](#Consciousness "Contents") that associates patterns of neuron activations with human-understandable
concepts.[[281]](#Computationalism_and_functionalism "Contents")


#### Bad actors and weaponised AI

Main articles: [Lethal autonomous weapon](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents"), [Artificial intelligence arms race](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents"), and [AI safety](#Transhumanism "Contents")
Artificial intelligence provides a number of tools that are useful to [bad actors](#Transhumanism "Contents"), such as [authoritarian governments](#Transhumanism "Contents"), [terrorists](#In_fiction "Contents"), [criminals](#In_fiction "Contents") or [rogue states](#See_also "Contents").

A lethal autonomous weapon is a machine that locates, selects and engages human targets
without human supervision.[[q]](#Further_reading "Contents") Widely available AI
tools can be used by bad actors to develop inexpensive autonomous weapons and, if
produced at scale, they are potentially [weapons of mass destruction](#Textbooks "Contents").[[283]](#Other_sources "Contents")
Even when used in conventional warfare, they currently cannot reliably choose targets
and could potentially [kill an innocent person](#External_links "Contents").[[283]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-dropdown-checkbox ")
In 2014, 30 nations (including China) supported a ban on autonomous weapons under
the [United Nations](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-unpinned-container")' [Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-unpinned-container"), however the [United States](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "vector-unpinned-container") and others
disagreed.[[284]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunsmatige_intelligensie "Kunsmatige intelligensie – Afrikaans")
By 2015, over fifty countries were reported to be researching battlefield robots.[[285]](https://als.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%BCnstliche_Intelligenz "Künstliche Intelligenz – Alemannic")

AI tools make it easier for authoritarian governments to efficiently control their
citizens in several ways. Face and [voice recognition](gsw "Künstliche Intelligenz") allow widespread [surveillance](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%88%B0%E1%8B%8D_%E1%88%A0%E1%88%AB%E1%88%BD_%E1%8B%A8%E1%88%9B%E1%88%B0%E1%89%A5_%E1%89%BD%E1%88%8E%E1%89%B3 "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic"). [Machine learning](am "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ – Amharic"), operating this data, can [classify](am "ሰው ሠራሽ የማሰብ ችሎታ") potential enemies of the state and prevent them from hiding. [Recommendation systems](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelichencia_artificial "Intelichencia artificial – Aragonese") can precisely target [propaganda](an "Intelichencia artificial") and [misinformation](https://anp.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AE_%E0%A4%AC%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%BF "कृत्रिम बुद्धि – Angika") for maximum effect. [Deepfakes](anp "कृत्रिम बुद्धि – Angika") and [generative AI](anp "कृत्रिम बुद्धि – Angika") aid in producing misinformation. Advanced AI can make authoritarian [centralised decision-making](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%A1_%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic") more competitive than liberal and decentralised systems such as [markets](ar "ذكاء اصطناعي – Arabic"). It lowers the cost and difficulty of [digital warfare](https://ary.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%AF%D9%83%D8%A7_%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan Arabic") and [advanced spyware](https://ary.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%AF%D9%83%D8%A7_%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A "دكا صطيناعي – Moroccan
Arabic").[[286]](https://as.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A7%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE_%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese")
All these technologies have been available since 2020 or earlier—AI [facial recognition systems](as "কৃত্ৰিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা – Assamese") are already being used for [mass surveillance](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelixencia_artificial "Intelixencia artificial – Asturian") in
China.[[287]](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%BCni_intellekt "Süni intellekt –
Azerbaijani")[[288]](https://azb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D9%85%D8%B5%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B9%DB%8C_%D8%B0%DA%A9%D8%A7 "مصنوعی ذکا – South Azerbaijani")

There are many other ways in which AI is expected to help bad actors, some of which
can not be foreseen. For example, machine-learning AI is able to design tens of thousands
of toxic molecules in a matter of hours.[[289]](https://bat-smg.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%97rbt%C4%97ns_intelekts "Dėrbtėns intelekts – Samogitian")


#### Technological unemployment

Main articles: [Workplace impact of artificial intelligence](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%87%D0%BD%D1%8B_%D1%96%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%8D%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%82 "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian") and [Technological unemployment](be "Штучны інтэлект – Belarusian")
Economists have frequently highlighted the risks of redundancies from AI, and speculated
about unemployment if there is no adequate social policy for full employment.[[290]](https://bh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%9F%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AB%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B2_%E0%A4%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%9F%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%B8 "आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस – Bhojpuri")

In the past, technology has tended to increase rather than reduce total employment,
but economists acknowledge that "we're in uncharted territory" with AI.[[291]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")
A survey of economists showed disagreement about whether the increasing use of robots
and AI will cause a substantial increase in long-term [unemployment](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles"), but they generally agree that it could be a net benefit if [productivity](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") gains are [redistributed](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ext.globalCssJs.user.styles").[[292]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
Risk estimates vary; for example, in the 2010s, Michael Osborne and [Carl Benedikt Frey](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") estimated 47% of U.S. jobs are at "high risk" of potential automation, while an OECD report classified only 9% of U.S. jobs as "high
risk".[[r]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia")[[294]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
The methodology of speculating about future employment levels has been criticised
as lacking evidential foundation, and for implying that technology, rather than social
policy, creates unemployment, as opposed to redundancies.[[290]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
In April 2023, it was reported that 70% of the jobs for Chinese video game illustrators
had been eliminated by generative artificial intelligence.[[295]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence -
Wikipedia")[[296]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
Early-career workers showed decreasing [employment rates](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") in some AI-exposed
occupations.[[297]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")

Unlike previous waves of automation, many middle-class jobs may be eliminated by
artificial intelligence; *[The Economist](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")*
stated in 2015 that "the worry that AI could do to white-collar jobs what steam power
did to blue-collar ones during the Industrial Revolution" is "worth taking seriously".[[298]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia")
Jobs at extreme risk range from [paralegals](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") to fast food cooks, while job demand is likely to increase for care-related professions ranging from personal healthcare to the
clergy.[[299]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia") In
July 2025, [Ford](/static/apple-touch/wikipedia.png "Wikipedia (en)") CEO [Jim Farley](/w/rest.php/v1/search "Wikipedia (en)") predicted that "artificial intelligence is going to replace literally half of all [white-collar workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Wikipedia Atom feed") in the
U.S."[[300]](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=")

From the early days of the development of artificial intelligence, there have been
arguments, for example, those put forward by [Joseph Weizenbaum](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class="), who developed the [ELIZA](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=") chatbot between 1964 and 1966, about whether tasks that can be done by computers actually should be done by them, given the difference between computers and humans, and between quantitative calculation and qualitative, value-based
judgement.[[301]](#bodyContent "></script></head>
<body class=")


#### Substitution for human–human interaction

See also: [Deaths linked to chatbots](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu")
With the increase of [loneliness](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") in the early 21st century, AI is sometimes identified as a potential source of relief to this problem. It would be possible, via [human-like qualities built into AI products](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page
[z]"),[[302]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") for individuals to assume
that this need can be met by artificial means.[[303]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page
[z]")[[304]](/wiki/Wikipedia:Contents "Guides to browsing Wikipedia") In some cases,
people approach artificial intelligence for companionship when they believe that
they would not find acceptance due to feeling outcast.[[305]](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us "How to contact Wikipedia")
Examples of harm coming to humans from advanced [chatbots](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia") have been reported in courts in the United States, with AI companies accused of creating products that endanger humans through [emotional confusion or deception](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Guidance on how to use and edit
Wikipedia").[[306]](/wiki/Wikipedia:File_upload_wizard "A list of recent changes to Wikipedia
[r]")[[307]](/wiki/Main_Page "Search Wikipedia [f]")


#### Existential risk

Main article: [Existential risk from artificial intelligence](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
Recent public debates in artificial intelligence have increasingly focused on its
broader societal and ethical implications. It has been argued AI will become so powerful
that humanity may irreversibly lose control of it. This could, as physicist [Stephen Hawking](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]") stated, "[spell the end of the human race](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia
[f]")".[[308]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
This scenario has been common in science fiction, when a computer or robot suddenly
develops a human-like "self-awareness" (or "sentience" or "consciousness") and becomes
a malevolent character.[[s]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
These sci-fi scenarios are misleading in several ways.

First, AI does not require human-like [sentience](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") to be an existential risk. Modern AI programs are given specific goals and use learning and intelligence to achieve them. Philosopher [Nick Bostrom](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=") argued that if one gives
*almost any* goal to a sufficiently powerful AI, it may choose to destroy humanity
to achieve it (he used the example of an [automated paperclip factory](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence "You are encouraged to create an account and log in; however, it is not mandatory") that destroys the world to get more iron for
paperclips).[[310]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")
[Stuart Russell](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") gives the example of household robot that tries to find a way to kill its owner to prevent it from being unplugged, reasoning that "you can't fetch the coffee if you're
dead."[[311]](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=")
In order to be safe for humanity, a [superintelligence](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=") would have to be genuinely [aligned](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Artificial+intelligence " title=") with humanity's morality and values so that it is "fundamentally on our
side".[[312]](# "Contents")

Second, [Yuval Noah Harari](# "Contents") argues that AI does not require a robot body or physical control to pose an existential risk. The essential parts of civilisation are not physical. Things like [ideologies](# "Contents"), [law](# "Contents"), [government](# "Contents"), [money](# "Contents") and the [economy](# "Contents") are built on [language](# "Contents"); they exist because there are stories that billions of people believe. The current prevalence of [misinformation](# "Contents") suggests that an AI could use language to convince people to believe anything, even to take actions that are
destructive.[[313]](#Reasoning_and_problem-solving "Contents") Geoffrey Hinton said
in 2025 that [modern AI](#Knowledge_representation "Contents") is particularly "good at persuasion" and getting better all the time. He asks, "Suppose you wanted to invade the capital of the US. Do you have to go there and do it yourself? No. You just have to be good at
persuasion."[[314]](#Learning "Contents")

The opinions amongst experts and industry insiders are mixed, with sizeable fractions
both concerned and unconcerned by risk from eventual superintelligent AI.[[315]](#General_intelligence "Contents")
Personalities such as Stephen Hawking, [Bill Gates](#General_intelligence "Contents"), and [Elon Musk](#Techniques
"Contents"),[[316]](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents") as well as AI pioneers
such as [Geoffrey Hinton](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents"), [Yoshua Bengio](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents"), [Stuart Russell](#Search_and_optimisation "Contents"), [Demis Hassabis](#State_space_search "Contents"), and [Sam Altman](#State_space_search "Contents"), have expressed concerns about existential risk from AI.

In May 2023, Geoffrey Hinton announced his resignation from Google in order to be
able to "freely speak out about the risks of AI" without "considering how this impacts
Google".[[317]](#Logic "Contents") He notably mentioned risks of an [AI takeover](#Logic
"Contents"),[[318]](#Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning "Contents") and
stressed that in order to avoid the worst outcomes, establishing safety guidelines
will require cooperation among those competing in use of AI.[[319]](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents")

In 2023, many leading AI experts endorsed [the joint statement](#Artificial_neural_networks "Contents") that "Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear
war".[[320]](#Hardware_and_software "Contents")

Some other researchers were more optimistic. AI pioneer [Jürgen Schmidhuber](#Applications "Contents") did not sign the joint statement, emphasising that in 95% of all cases, AI research is about making "human lives longer and healthier and
easier."[[321]](#AI-assisted_software_development "Contents") While the tools that
are now being used to improve lives can also be used by bad actors, "they can also
be used against the bad actors."[[322]](#Chatbots "Contents")[[323]](#Health_and_medicine "Contents")
[Andrew Ng](#Health_and_medicine "Contents") also argued that "it's a mistake to fall for the doomsday hype on AI—and that regulators who do will only benefit vested
interests."[[324]](#Mathematics "Contents") [Yann LeCun](#Mathematics "Contents"), a Turing Award winner, disagreed with the idea that AI will subordinate humans "simply because they are smarter, let alone destroy
[us]",[[325]](#Military "Contents") "scoff[ing] at his peers' dystopian scenarios
of supercharged misinformation and even, eventually, human extinction." In contrast,
he claimed that "intelligent machines will usher in a new renaissance for humanity,
a new era of enlightenment."[[326]](#Agents "Contents") In the early 2010s, experts
argued that the risks are too distant in the future to warrant research or that humans
will be valuable from the perspective of a superintelligent machine.[[327]](#Sexuality "Contents")
However, after 2016, the study of current and future risks and possible solutions
became a serious area of research.[[328]](#Risks_and_harm "Contents")


### Ethical machines and alignment

Main articles: [Machine ethics](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents"), [AI safety](#Power_needs_and_environmental_impacts "Contents"), [Friendly artificial intelligence](#Misinformation "Contents"), [Artificial moral agents](#Misinformation "Contents"), and [Human Compatible](#Misinformation "Contents")

See also: [Human–AI interaction](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents")
Friendly AI are machines that have been designed from the beginning to minimise risks
and to make choices that benefit humans. [Eliezer Yudkowsky](#Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI "Contents"), who coined the term, argues that developing friendly AI should be a higher research priority: it may require a large investment and it must be completed before AI becomes an existential
risk.[[329]](#Existential_risk "Contents")

Machines with intelligence have the potential to use their intelligence to make ethical
decisions. The field of machine ethics provides machines with ethical principles
and procedures for resolving ethical dilemmas.[[330]](#Frameworks "Contents")The
field of machine ethics is also called computational morality,[[330]](#Philosophy "Contents")and
was founded at an [AAAI](#Defining_artificial_intelligence "Contents") symposium in 2005.[[331]](#Legal_definitions "Contents")

Other approaches include [Wendell Wallach](#Evaluating_approaches_to_AI "Contents")'s "artificial moral
agents"[[332]](#Neat_vs._scruffy "Contents") and [Stuart J. Russell](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents")'s [three principles](#Soft_vs._hard_computing "Contents") for developing provably beneficial
machines.[[333]](#Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind "Contents")


### Open source

See also: [Open-source artificial intelligence](#AI_welfare_and_rights "Contents") and [Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software](#Future "Contents")
Active organisations in the AI open-source community include [Hugging Face](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity
"Contents"),[[334]](#Superintelligence_and_the_singularity "Contents") [Google](#Transhumanism
